title: Once A Day Dynasty, Now Live Beta, Stake Your Claim
author: certaintyisuncertain
selftext:
Once A Day Dynasty is a grand strategy game in a massively multiplayer persistent shared world.   
  
It's a game I've been working on in one way or another for over 10 years.

This latest version was reworked thanks to the help of Claude Code to get it off of PHP, which was severely limiting it.

It's now live. [You can stake your claims and start to build your kingdom.](https://onceadaydynasty.com/) You can also engage in the forums both in role-play sections and meta-game sections.

You might remember that I posted a game here House & Dominion (also called Reign and Record... why does AI love "something & something" titles so much?) awhile back that was a similar concept but focused mainly on answer citizens in a throne room and trying to rule a solar system House (kind of link Dune). I had posted here about developing it with Repit over about 30 days. It was a little more sloppy than I would have liked and the LLM costs in-game were too high.

Once A Day Dynasty now is both of those ideas merged together. 

I took the parts that were working from House & Dominion and scraped the parts that weren't. I merged that with what had worked previously with my Once Daily Risk and Nation Builder games that are not retired for a few years. 

This also takes lot of inspiration from the two games I've sunk the most time into: Civilization and Total War.

Honestly in testing I spent probably an extra month while I still had my finger on the "advance to next year" button that no longer exists. I just couldn't stop myself from playing turn after turn after turn against the computers and the few friends that have been testing with me. For us at least it's so fun already. Lots more that we want to do, but even as is I'm always itching for the next day for another turn.

**Current Build Process:**   
\- Claude Code Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 (My job is to vibe code B2B software, so this is a really fun use case for that skill set in my 'free' time).  
\- Graphics are all CSS or SVGs so that they load fast and are scalable. They're either hand "drawn" by me or Claude (usually a bit of both) and some use SVGMaker Agent, which has been great.  
\- UI is all Claude with my feedback. It's something I definitely want to take another crack at here soon.  
\- Demo version in an artifact in Claude that I can rapidly iterate on and test.   
\- What's working there then gets created as work-branches that can be tested in the web and on mobile.  
\- Then it gets shipped to the real game with the persistent world.

***Happy to answer any questions or take feedback.***   
  
If you do try out the game, use the little sun icon on the right side that has your settings to find the IDEAS AND THE FORUM section. I'd love to hear your ideas and feedback.

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: Update your UI if you want anyone to be interested

replies.author: Excellent_Space_2178
replies.body: I second this. This looks too much like cookie cutter Claude output. In this example you wouldn’t even need to make your own art. Literally “asking” for a different font would be enough.

replies.author: certaintyisuncertain
replies.body:
Both fair. As I said in the description, that's one of the things I'll be taking a crack at next.

People are already playing it though, so it's not really a blocker for starting to play.

I hear you though, I don't like the look of the UI either. We'll see what I can do in the next few days. 

Any specific advice on how you're handling UI though Claude Code?

replies.author: Excellent_Space_2178
replies.body: Glad to hear people are already playing. Take concrete notes on what it is that you do not like about the UI. Study other similar games and general readability. Generate breakdowns and comparisons, and, completely optional, hand write a font. Human art goes a long way in the age of GenAI slop

replies.author: certaintyisuncertain
replies.body: Thanks appreciate the ideas. I've done some hand-drawing of some of the other design elements. So that's an interesting idea. I do that a lot at work too to get something that feels more unique.
